chunks: And through it, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa and al-Hasan ibn Dhareef, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'We narrate that the master of this command will be hidden for a period, so what will we do in that case?' He said: 'Hold fast to the previous matter that you are upon until it becomes clear to you.'

key_terms.حَتَّى يَبِينَ لَكُمْ: Until it becomes clear to you
key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of Command (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What should Muslims do during the Imam's occultation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* addresses the theological anxiety surrounding the Imam's disappearance by instructing believers to maintain steadfastness in the established religious order ('the first matter') until the truth is revealed. It underscores the Shia principle of continuity in religious authority during the occultation, emphasizing patience and adherence to established norms as a safeguard against confusion or innovation.
